stem:
Fig. 5.1 shows a pendulum consisting of a metal sphere suspended by a thin string.

[[fig:f1]]

The sphere undergoes small oscillations about its equilibrium position. The oscillations may be considered to be simple harmonic.

Fig. 5.2 shows the variation with time *t* of the displacement *x* of the sphere from its equilibrium position.

[[fig:f2]]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: On Fig. 5.1, draw an arrow, from the centre of the sphere, to represent the direction of the resultant force acting on the sphere when it is in the position shown.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead: The mass of the sphere is 0.15 kg.
parts.text: State the amplitude of the oscillations.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the angular frequency of the oscillations.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the total energy of the oscillations.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
On Fig. 5.3, sketch the variation with *x* of the kinetic energy *E*ₖ of the sphere.

[[fig:f3]]

figures.caption: Fig. 5.1 (not to scale)
figures.alt: A metal sphere hangs from a thin string attached to a support, with a curved arrow indicating oscillations.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.2
figures.alt: A displacement–time graph shows a sinusoidal oscillation with displacement between approximately −0.016 m and 0.016 m over 1.2 s.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.3
figures.alt: A blank graph grid has displacement x in metres on the horizontal axis and kinetic energy Eₖ in units of 10⁻³ J on the vertical axis.
